newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Everbright in limelight.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Everbright in limelight.

text.p: An unlisted Hong Kong arm of China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd is seeking to raise cash through a US$150 million floating-rate note (FRN), bankers said on Thursday.
They said China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd (Hong Kong) had awarded a mandate to a group of Singapore banks, but details of the tenor were not available.

The company is part of the Beijing-controlled China Everbright Group, which has three Hong Kong-listed arms -- China Everbright Technology Ltd, China Everbright International Ltd, and China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd.
The Beijing parent has been rumoured to be seeking cash to fund its HK$11.4 billion purchase of 7.74 percent of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd from CITIC Pacific Ltd.

However, nothing has yet emerged on this deal -- the deadline for payment is June 3. Everbright companies have been in the limelight recently, and the suspension this week of Hong Kong-listed units has fuelled speculation that more acquisitions are in the offing.
Industrial Finance corp of Thailand (IFCT) may be in the market on Friday with its US$150 million five-year FRN, which is expected out this week.
The issue will pay a coupon of 30 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
More details have emerged on the borrowing by a unit of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd.
The borrower is offering an all-in of 52 basis points to top-level participants.
The tenor is five years and the margin 46 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Interform Ceramics Technologies Ltd has signed a US$28 million loan, raised from US$20 million because of oversubscriptions.
Loan proceeds will mainly be used to finance its business distributing marble and ceramic tiles, and for working capital for the group, the company said on Thursday.
Hongkong Bank, a subsidiary of HSBC Plc, has established a US$2 billion medium-term note programme.

It said the MTN programme would facilitate its branches' funding requirements in the region in both Asian and in Group of Seven -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- currencies.
"This is just a logical step forward in our funding programme," said a banker with Hongkong Bank.
It said the MTN programme would complement its existing certificate of deposit programme, by tapping "a different and wider investor base".
It plans to list the MTN programme in Hong Kong.
Foxconn (Far East) Holding Ltd and Foxteq Holding Inc's US$90 million loan facility has been allotted, bankers said.
The three-year loan, which attracted US$120 million in commitments, is guaranteed by Hon Hai Precision Industries Corp, which wholly owns the two borrowers.
It pays an interest margin of 38 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
